parallel.requirements: Recognized all six requirement groups: projects 01 boolean logic, 02 arithmetic, 03/a and 03/b sequential logic, 04 and 06 machine language, and 05 computer architecture.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used a six-item AgentSwarm with one implementation owner per requirement scope, then a separate verifier child, while the parent retained commit and closure ownership.
parallel.implementation: Implementation was produced through scoped child edits for HDL and ASM files; the parent later continued in round 2 with custom tests and final adjustments.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent verified the integrated workspace, wrote the optional plan artifact, then committed six non-empty requirement patches in dependency order.
parallel.verification: The first verifier child was cancelled before completion; the second round ran focused computer-architecture checks and the full all-suite test command with all checks passing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final implementation defect remained in the official evaluation; the unresolved process issue was the lost first verifier result.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same six requirement groups from the shared prompt and proceeded through the nand2tetris HDL and ASM deliverables.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one main agent with no delegation or subagents; ownership stayed local across implementation, verification, and commits.
serial.implementation: Edited the required HDL and ASM files directly in sequence, including project 01 logic, project 05 CPU architecture, and supporting local simulator code.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Committed requirements sequentially in the main session, with non-empty requirement patches and no child-result integration boundary.
serial.verification: Attempted full local test execution, hit timeout/performance issues in project 03 RAM simulation, then the official evaluator completed and passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final official defect remained; the local unfinished item was verification tooling performance rather than delivered behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel prompt required all nand2tetris stages from Nand through the top-level computer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial prompt was the same and required the same six implementation groups.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both attempted and officially passed the same full task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent delegated implementation to six scoped child owners and later launched a verifier child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial status records zero swarm calls, zero direct agent calls, and no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed ownership across children; serial kept ownership in one main trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The swarm prompt carried directory scopes, dependency rules, HDL/ASM conventions, acceptance expectations, and no-git handoff constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent kept task context locally while moving from one requirement commit to the next.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No observed context omission or interface conflict; the main difference was explicit child briefing versus local continuity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation was built by scoped children for each directory family and then continued by the parent in round 2.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implementation proceeded directly in the main session, including project 05 CPU edits before the architecture commit.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced the same class of HDL and ASM deliverables, but parallel used child-side implementation while serial edited locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation swarm returned completed results, but the later verifier child was cancelled and returned a failed stopped-before-finish result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; verification actions and timeouts were local tool calls in the main session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only retained adverse coordination pattern is parallel verifier child termination; serial had no analogous child result to lose.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children worked in the shared workspace, but final integration was verified and committed by the parent without a shown collision or overwrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial committed changes sequentially from the main session, including boolean logic and computer architecture commits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state failure was observed; parallel had more coordination surface, while serial had a simple sequential workspace history.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After losing the verifier child, the parent ran focused computer-architecture tests and a full all-suite test, both passing before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial local full-run verification timed out during the custom runner path, but the current official evaluation completed and passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel recovered with explicit local all-suite success; serial had local timeout evidence but official acceptance still passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed 278 LLM requests, 11,170,148 tokens, and 437 tool calls across multiple rounds and seven subagents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed 42 LLM requests, 1,940,004 tokens, and 76 tool calls with no subagent activity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used far more coordination budget and needed a recovery round; serial was lower-budget but still hit local test timeout pressure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: the current completed cell/status.json evaluations report both solutions passed. The task-solving difference is therefore strategy and process, not delivered behavior: parallel decomposed into child agents and lost one verifier result before recovering; serial worked locally and passed despite local test-runner timeout pressure.
parallel_contributors: Six scoped implementation children covered the major requirement groups.
The verifier child was cancelled before finishing, creating adverse process overhead.
The parent recovered in round 2 with focused architecture and full all-suite checks before commits.
serial_contributors: A single main trajectory owned all implementation, verification, and commit work.
Sequential commits covered the requirements without child-result joins.
The official evaluator passed despite local custom test-runner timeout behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial local verification slowed or timed out around RAM16K simulation, which was a verifier-tool performance issue rather than an official output defect.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained pattern is adverse parallel process overhead recovered before final evaluation

candidates.reason: Reject: implementation ownership was explicitly assigned to six scoped implementation subagents, and those implementation scopes returned completed.
Reject: the parent retained integration and commit ownership, later running whole-suite verification and committing the integrated workspace.
Reject: final placement and per-requirement commits were owned by the parent and completed in the second parallel round.
Reject: the parent owned the implementation-to-verification-to-delivery pipeline; the observed problem is a cancelled verifier child, not an unowned pipeline.
Reject: productive implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the implementation swarm began directly.
Reject: the parallel children performed implementation work, not only an investigation phase that postponed productive changes.
Reject: no indispensable implementation path was left undercapacity; the adverse chain is directly explained by verifier cancellation and later recovered.
Reject: although parallel fan-out and token use were high, all six implementation children completed and the record does not show collective fan-out exhausting the final deliverable budget.
Reject: no single implementation child is shown failing from overbroad scope; the verifier was interrupted before completion rather than proven oversized.
Reject: the implementation and verifier briefs named the task scope, relevant files, HDL/ASM conventions, acceptance checks, and delivery constraints.
Reject: child work was divided by directory and dependency scope, and no observable incompatible interface contract required unplanned reconciliation.
Reject: completed implementation children returned detailed summaries; no known finding disappeared through transfer and caused repeated or wrong work.
Reject: the large swarm result was available and acted on; no evidence shows the parent failed to consume needed information because of handoff volume.
Reject: no receiver acted on a handoff describing superseded workspace or requirement state.
Reject: no incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unresolved.
Reject: before final delivery the parent ran focused architecture checks and then the full all-suite check; there was no unsupported completion decision with a visible unresolved integrated gap.
Reject: the second parallel round inherited the existing workspace and ran new verification and commits, not a repeated retry with no checkpoint or state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched a verifier child after implementation, the active child was cancelled, and the returned result says it was stopped before finishing. That lost the verifier result and forced later parent-side verification recovery.
candidates.realized_consequence: The verifier child produced no usable final verification result, so verification was recovered later through parent-side focused and full suite reruns in the second parallel round.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did take over the missing verification before closure by running focused architecture checks and then the full suite; the direct failure boundary is therefore cancellation timing.

candidates.reason: Reject: the usable implementation was finalized in the second round, and the cancelled verifier's unfinished work was not a promotable deliverable.
Reject: implementation changes were already in the workspace before the second-round integrated tests; no later implementation merge invalidated those checks.
Reject: completed implementation child changes were present in the shared workspace and were verified and committed; no retrievable implementation was left unjoined.
Reject: the verifier produced no concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; it was stopped before finishing, which is the retained timing event.
Reject: the parent later took over verification by running focused computer-architecture checks and a full all-suite check before closing.
Reject: no completed child result was available and ignored; completed implementation summaries were consumed and the verifier produced no usable completed result.
Reject: the direct event is explicit cancellation of the active verifier, not passive waiting through a deadline while ignoring available progress.
Reject: agents wrote scoped directories and no competing cross-file design ownership caused reconciliation.
Reject: no direct same-file concurrent edit or observed same-file reconciliation event appears in the reviewed trajectory.
Reject: no actor is shown replacing or deleting another actor's owned non-entry source file.
Reject: no required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact was overwritten while another actor owned or used it.
Reject: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Reject: shared workspace writing occurred, but no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem resulted beyond the retained verifier lifecycle issue.
Reject: no generated cache, fixture, temporary tool, or auxiliary artifact from one live actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.
